entries.clue: Consuming more rum, English doctor's a feeble sort (8)

indicators.note: the doctor eats the other letters, so they end up inside him

blocks.note: DR = doctor, opened up to take the rest in
rum = odd, so more rum = odder

annotation.surface: A heavy-drinking English doctor is written off as a weakling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink; here it is the old adjective meaning strange, so 'more rum' is ODDER, which goes inside DR along with E.
annotation.definitionFit: A dodderer is someone shaky and frail, a feeble sort.

entries.clue: No advantage to be seen in Blue Team (8)

annotation.surface: A sports pundit says the Blue team has no edge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue Team' reads as a club's colours, and blue here is the feeling, not the kit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drawback is the reverse of an upside, so it offers no advantage.

entries.clue: A spreading of legs on vacation ruined with despair (9)

indicators.note: a word that has been vacated keeps only its outside letters
the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: LEGS emptied of its middle leaves L…S

annotation.surface: A holiday ruined, legs sprawled out in despair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of legs' looks like part of the definition, a spreading of legs; the definition stops at 'A spreading', and legs is emptied to LS for the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scattering things over a wide area is spreading them.

entries.clue: Bunch of footballers still gaining weight (7)

annotation.surface: Footballers who are still putting on weight.
annotation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club, so the 'bunch of footballers' is a whole team.
annotation.definitionFit: Everton is an English Premier League football club.

entries.clue: As an aristocrat might be advanced (5)

blocks.note: a noble title plus the adjective ending -Y, 'like a peer'
advanced in the sense of ahead of time

annotation.surface: A description of how a nobleman might carry himself.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a made-up word: EARL plus the adjective ending -Y, 'earl-ish'. Only the second half uses the real word.
annotation.definitionFit: Early means before the usual time, advanced as in an advanced or early stage.

entries.clue: Is not good to frame House leader? How disappointing! (6)

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so SUCKS goes round H
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: sucks = is no good, in slang

annotation.surface: A political complaint that the Commons leader is being stitched up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House leader' looks like a parliamentary title; it is just the H that starts House.
annotation.definitionFit: Shucks is an exclamation of mild disappointment.

entries.clue: A one-time politician opens shelter – that's fishy (7)

indicators.note: the politician forces the hut open and sits inside it

blocks.note: LIB = Liberal, the party the Liberal Democrats replaced

annotation.surface: A former MP moves into a shed, and something smells off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's fishy' sounds like suspicion; taken literally it is the definition, something that is a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a twist: 'fishy' usually means suspect, but here it means literally a fish, and the flatfish qualifies.

entries.clue: Intimate feature on top of abdomen (5)

definitions.note: 'Intimate' is a noun here: a close friend

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the chin is a facial feature

annotation.surface: A body part placed intimately on top of a belly.
annotation.walkthrough: CHINA is rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a china is a close friend.
annotation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a china (plate) is a mate, an intimate friend.

entries.clue: Starmer's intitial backing of No. 10 uprising is something out of Shakespeare? (6)

indicators.note: misprinted 'initial'; the initial of a word is its first letter
in a down answer, rising means read from the bottom up

annotation.surface: Keir Starmer backing a revolt in Downing Street sounds like a Shakespeare plot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No. 10' looks like Downing Street, the Prime Minister's house; read as NO and TEN, each rises to ON and NET under the S.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Shakespeare wrote 154 of these fourteen-line poems, but so did many others.

entries.clue: Looked back on gutless Trumpite's "Kill!" (5)

indicators.note: to look back is to face the other way, so the word for looked is read from right to left
a word with its guts removed keeps only the outer letters

blocks.note: looked = SAW, turned back to WAS
TRUMPITE with its insides gone leaves T…E

annotation.surface: A MAGA supporter's cry for blood, and someone looking back on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kill' is in quotes to look like the Trumpite's words; it is the definition, as in slang 'waste someone'.
annotation.definitionFit: To waste someone is slang for killing them.

entries.clue: Nellie's heart put into collapsing boner – 'revolting thing!' (9)

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle
ELLI goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of BONER fall apart and settle in a new order

blocks.note: NELLIE without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Nellie is disgusted by a wilting erection.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits inside quotation marks and reads as Nellie's reaction; 'revolting' means rising up, not disgusting.
annotation.definitionFit: A rebellion is a revolt, a revolting thing in the uprising sense.

entries.clue: Toby gets wallop on face (4,3)

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another comes first

blocks.note: wallop is British slang for beer

annotation.surface: Someone called Toby gets punched in the face.
annotation.walkthrough: Toby looks like a man's name; a Toby jug is a pottery drinking mug shaped like a seated man, so Toby is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a traditional beer mug moulded as a figure in a tricorn hat.

entries.clue: 'Kindly piss in street,' put heartlessly (7)

indicators.note: piss in the street is literally inside it, so the word for piss goes inside the abbreviation for street
LAY loses its heart, the middle A

blocks.note: put = LAY, minus its middle A

annotation.surface: A polite sign asking people to urinate in the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kindly' reads as part of the request, as in 'kindly do this'; it is the definition, meaning in a kind way.
annotation.definitionFit: Sweetly and kindly both mean in a gentle, pleasant manner.

entries.clue: Dash! Underwear can't expand openings for intimate contact (7)

indicators.note: the openings of words are their first letters

blocks.note: an em is a dash in printing, the em dash

annotation.surface: Frustration that a tight bra won't give during a cuddle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dash!' reads as a mild curse; it is the printer's EM dash.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hug is the closest bodily contact short of sex.

entries.clue: Fake news: 'HELL LINED UP!' (14)

blocks.note: Dis is the underworld in Roman myth and in Dante

annotation.surface: A tabloid screams that the gates of hell are opening.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a headline; read literally, Dis (hell) is IN FORMATION (lined up).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deliberately false reports spread to mislead are fake news.

entries.clue: Ignored love wearing gloves (7)

blocks.note: love = O, a zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: A spurned lover who always wears gloves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like it wants O put inside something; it belongs with 'gloves', and the whole phrase is the adjective MITTED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something left out has been passed over, ignored.

entries.clue: Crude oil money given to crafty southern Russians? (9)

indicators.note: crude oil is unrefined, so its letters are rough and rearranged

annotation.surface: Oil money handed to shady Russians.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: not all Russians are oligarchs, but oligarchs are typically Russians enriched by oil.
annotation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are the super-rich Russian businessmen who grew rich from oil and gas.

entries.clue: They protect members apt to be bent and keep working on head of state (4-4)

definitions.text: They protect members apt to be bent

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement
the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Politicians who kneel to the head of state and keep their jobs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link joining definition and wordplay; it is part of the anagram. Members here are limbs, the knees, apt to be bent.
annotation.definitionFit: Knee-pads protect knees, the limbs that bend.

entries.clue: Political delaying tactic is frustrating shitty act (8,6)

blocks.note: a motion is a bowel movement

annotation.surface: A complaint that parliamentary filibustering is a dirty trick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shitty' looks like mere abuse; it is literal, since a motion is also a bowel movement.
annotation.definitionFit: A blocking motion is a procedural motion used to stall business.

entries.clue: Mascara melted essentially, sweet (7)

indicators.note: the answer is in the essence, the inside, of the words

annotation.surface: Mascara running in the heat looks like something sweet.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the chewy toffee made from cooked sugar is a sweet, as British English calls a candy.

entries.clue: Best to limp off when shafted by one (7)

indicators.note: the letters of TO LIMP go off, gone bad and rearranged
a shaft driven in: one goes inside the anagram

annotation.surface: Advice that the best time to go limp is when you're being screwed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adverb; it is the definition, an adjective as in 'the best option'.
annotation.definitionFit: Optimal means best, most favourable.

entries.clue: Politician Pence's right to interrupt gentleman and smirk (6)

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a word is its last letter
to interrupt someone is to break into the middle of what they are saying, so these letters break into the middle of another word

annotation.surface: Mike Pence, the right-wing former US vice president, butts in on someone and smirks.
annotation.walkthrough: Pence looks like the US politician; only his last letter is used. 'Right' is not R here: it points to the end of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A simper is a coy, affected smile, close to a smirk.

entries.clue: Come by getting accepted by the woman before sexual activity (7)

annotation.surface: An innuendo about being welcomed into a woman's bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come by' reads as dropping in; it means acquire, and the pieces sit in clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: receiving property from someone who has died is one way to acquire it.

entries.clue: Really keen for it to be like part of the brass section? (5)

definitions.text: like part of the brass section

blocks.note: slang for sexually eager, 'it' being sex

blocks.clueFragment: like part of the brass section
blocks.note: a brass instrument's name plus the adjective ending -Y

annotation.surface: A trumpet player who is desperately keen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' is sex, so 'really keen for it' means aroused; the second half turns horn into an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Horny means sexually eager, and horn-y would mean like a horn.

entries.clue: Relentless striving produces nation of arses (3,4)

blocks.note: a rat, like an arse, is a contemptible person

annotation.surface: Cut-throat competition turns a country into a land of idiots.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'nation of arses' as 'race of rats', then put the rat first.
annotation.definitionFit: The rat race is the endless competitive struggle of working life.

entries.clue: Nixon 'hard going' on getting elected? Don't swallow that! (5)

indicators.note: HARD is going, leaving the name

blocks.note: Nixon's first name RICHARD with HARD gone

annotation.surface: Nixon found the election campaign hard going, and something is hard to swallow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard going' in quotes looks like a comment on Nixon's campaign; it tells you to drop HARD from RICHARD.
annotation.definitionFit: Ricin is a deadly poison, something never to swallow.

entries.clue: Penny has date in America, screwing member of ambulance crew (9)

indicators.note: P comes first and has the rest after it
a date in America is literally placed inside the country's name
the letters are twisted round into a new order

annotation.surface: Penny's American date involves an affair with an ambulance worker.
annotation.walkthrough: D is the standard abbreviation for date; put it in AMERICA and screw up the result.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the trained medic who rides the ambulance is part of its crew.

entries.clue: Brown's disapproving cry on getting in a state (5)

indicators.note: OCH gets inside the state's abbreviation

blocks.note: och is a Scottish cry of irritation

annotation.surface: Gordon Brown tuts in Scottish style when he gets worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: Brown looks like Gordon Brown, the Scottish former Prime Minister, which suits the Scots OCH; it is the colour.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the colour named after the coffee is a shade of brown.

entries.clue: King Brian and family impress greatly – gold all round! (6)

indicators.note: the whole thing is turned right round

annotation.surface: A fawning report that the King and his family were dazzling and won gold everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls King Charles 'Brian', so King Brian and family are the royals. SLAY then OR, and the whole of SLAYOR reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A magazine-specific name: Private Eye's nickname for King Charles is Brian, so he and his family make up the monarchy's household.

entries.clue: Like a bum unknown character having relative breakdown (8)

annotation.surface: A fussy layabout has a family meltdown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relative breakdown' reads as a family crisis; the break comes after 'relative', and breakdown means a detailed examination.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a close examination splits a thing into its parts, as a cost breakdown does.
